messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: region-rollout-checker triggered for rollout-eu-apac. 5xx spike in apac-west, latency surge. Paging @oncall-sre :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: On it, joining channel. grabbing alert details now.
laura-release: starting blue->green partial rollout to apac-west (~10% traffic). should be safe but seeing error spike right after flip. initial thought: DNS/edge mismatch.
marcus-sre: logs: 503s from model-backend (kv-cache miss explosion) + edge 524 timeouts. Graph: errors jump 6:02 -> 6:05 UTC.
laura-release: hmm, our rollout used shadow dns shard 'apac-shadow-1' with TTL 600s. some POPs still resolving old green, others to new blue -> mixed backend versions + incompatible cache keys.
amber-net: confirmed: geo-dns shard responded inconsistent NS set for a subset of APAC POPs. TTL fragmentation -> clients reusing old answers and hitting incompatible route.
oncall-sre: customer impact? which customers in apac?
marcus-sre: preliminary: ~12% of apac requests experienced 502/503. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Short-term: timeouts and model errors.
laura-release: mitigation plan: 1) kill the rollout flag (rollout-eu-apac -> OFF) 2) reduce DNS TTL to 30s and nudge DNS provider to refresh 3) purge edge KV cache entries for the rollout tag 4) rollback any partial image if flag doesn't stabilize.
oncall-sre: executing kill-switch now.
laura-release: command: `curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/api/keys/rollout-eu-apac/kill -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"`
deploy-bot: Feature flag rollout-eu-apac set to OFF by laura-release at 06:12:37 UTC.
oncall-sre: flag off, traffic should stop shifting. verifying routing table...
amber-net: lowering DNS TTL to 30s on apac zone (change submitted to provider). propagation expected within 60s for new queries but cached entries may persist until they expire.
marcus-sre: triggering edge cache purge for tag=apac-shadow-1 across POPs now:
```
kubectl -n edge exec deploy/edge-purger -- /bin/sh -c "purge --tag apac-shadow-1 --all-pops"
```
support-eng: purges started, reporting progress. some POPs finishing ~06:15 UTC.
marcus-sre: also kicking KV cache regen on model runtime to avoid stale state:
```
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart statefulset/kv-cache --selector=region=apac
```
laura-release: good. I'll monitor error rate and check for residual DNS skew. If errors don't fall under 1% within 5m, prepare rollback of the image tag.
noncall-sre: error rate falling: 12% -> 3% within 4m. latency normalizing for most POPs.
amber-net: provider confirms DNS TTL change accepted; new queries are 30s TTL. old cached will drop gradually.
laura-release: rolling back image not needed at this point. continue to monitor for 15m.
support-eng: CS notified: drafting outbound note for affected customers with rough impact and remediation steps.
cs-lead: thanks, please include timeline + mitigation + plan to credit for retryable errors.
marcus-sre: post-mortem notes for later: root cause = TTL fragmentation on shadow dns shard + incomplete KV cache compatibility between blue/green variants. Follow-ups: 1) enforce TTL <=60s for shard deployments, 2) validate edge KV key compatibility pre-rollout, 3) add automated canary health-check that validates both DNS and cache coherence.
incident-bot: Incident updated: SEV2 -> Mitigated. Assigned to laura-release for follow-up.
laura-release: prepping handoff: I'll create incident doc and timeline, handing off to @oncall-sre-night in 25m. will add customer impact summary.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. if anything regresses ping @oncall-sre immediately. :thumbsup:
support-eng: closing loop with CS and drafting credits.
cs-lead: good work, please make sure the PM and legal are notified if any SLA thresholds were breached.
laura-release: will do. closing channel in 30m after RCA draft.
incident-bot: Channel will be archived after 36 hours per policy.
